attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, after quoting an outside excerpt; the claim about OpenAI not disclosing is his.

semantics.note: 'Those numbers' refers to the water figures in the excerpt just before it. Dropping the GPT-5 remark is right: it is rhetorical and makes no forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'those numbers' as GPT-4 training-water figures follows the GPT-3 comparison. The window runs to the post date, and only a disclosure by OpenAI itself counts. This is a fair, ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Stanford assessment (Oct 2023) covered GPT-4 and found no company scored on broader environmental impact, which the paper says includes water use.
Water-footprint researchers (Oct 2023) estimated GPT-3 instead because public GPT-4 data was limited. Corroborates the gap.
OpenAI's own report withholds training details (hardware, compute, etc.). As a company document it is context, consistent with no water figure being disclosed.

reviews.rationale: Independent assessments from Oct 2023 found no OpenAI disclosure of GPT-4 water or environmental figures, and OpenAI's report withheld training details. No disclosure before Feb 10, 2024 appears in the packet. The independent sources end in Oct 2023, a small gap, but the contradiction condition is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps his wording 'pressure from GenAI' and the qualifier 'already'. It is a present-state observation.

contract.note: Requiring a documented generative-AI contribution follows his word 'GenAI'. The Jan to Feb 10, 2024 window is the evaluator's choice but reasonably matches 'already'. The result turns on separating generative AI from general data-center demand.

evidence.note: Secondary article (Feb 2024) based on Bloomberg. It links AI to Evergy's June 2023 coal delay only by speculation ('perhaps not coincidentally') and reports Dominion considering coal retention without showing a generative-AI cause.
Dominion's plan (May 2023) attributes demand growth to data centers generally. It predates the window and does not isolate generative AI, so it is not counterevidence.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows coal retention tied to data-center demand, but no readable primary record shows generative AI demand contributing during the target window. The key sources (Bloomberg, Evergy transcript) were unreadable. Nothing shows the pressure was absent either.
